Dear Students, Why do we learn art? Why practice it? It is only in a society which believes that the ability in art is inborn, that such questions arise. Yet, like any other subject in the humanities, art education too is a discipline that makes demands on our attention and intellect. This textbook, which covers painting, sculpture, music, dance, theatre and cinema, seeks to facilitate not just the production of knowledge related to these art forms, but also creative efforts in them. It goes beyond the conventional approach that focuses on the acquisition of artistic skills, usually undertaken in a competitive spirit. Its purpose is to creatively redefine the very process of education through a deeper understanding of the arts. In this text, we learn about those aspects of the arts - from painting to dance to theatre - that transcend geographical and historical boundaries.
In that sense, it also ushers us into the wider realm of human creativity itself. We look forward to your feedback and comments. With love and regards,

Master Amal Iqbal National Hand Wrestling Champion Amal Iqbal, a remarkable figure in national handicapped wrestling, demonstrated extraordinary self-confidence and resilience despite severe physical challenges. Stricken by cerebral palsy, he needed assistance in reading, writing and even eating until he was ten years old. It was difficult for him to speak and move. He overcame these challenges by self and became a famous person. He marked history in river rafting by successfully navigating Beas River in Himachal Pradesh and Tejaswini River in Kerala. Despite 90% of disabilities, Amal is a national-level hand-wrestling champion. His hard work fetched him two gold medals in hand wrestling and many other awards and honours. Amal Iqbal won the national story-writing competition organized by the Ganga Foundation, Coimbatore for students with cerebral palsy.

Shalin Survivor, Entrepreneur At the age of 35, as a single parent to two teenagers, Shalin started her life from scratch. At this time, she was facing the possibility of cancer for the second time and was under treatment She encountered massive challenges like financial crisis, unemployment and lack of support from family, friends and community. Despite facing adversities, Shalin took on various roles, from being a caretaker for a friend's mother to working as a customer relations officer at star hotels and as a hospitality trainer. It was her proficiency to speak multiple languages and her education that enabled her to explore these opportunities.
However, being a single independent woman in those days, brought hardships and she had to face various exploitations which made her switch jobs frequently. It

was tough for her, especially during her treatment period and times of natural disasters like floods, Okhi etc. as the disasters negatively impacted the hospitality industry. She started an initiative called "Ente Chottu Paathram " to provide nutritious meals for three children who regularly had only lemon juice and puffs for lunch. Over a period of time, she managed to expand this initiative and now provides high-quality meals for approximately two hundred people at minimal rates. Inspired by her efforts, other women also began this venture of serving food to those in need and run their business ventures successfully. Beyond her struggles, Shalin actively engages in various social and cultural activities. During the time of flood, she played a crucial role in the ‘Oppamund Thiruvananthapuram’ project. Many projects that support and uplift transgenders and differently-abled children are being planned and implemented by her.

One of Shalin's remarkable contributions is empowering forty mothers of autistic children to become entrepreneurs. Despite challenges such as disease, exploitation, exclusion and financial instability, Shalin inspires many. Her resilience in the phase of adversity, has made her a role model for her daughter, who is now a doctor, and her son, who is an engineer. Adam Harry First Trans man Pilot Adam Harry held a profound fascination for the sky and airplanes even from a very young age. A toy aeroplane which was gifted to little Adam kindled zir ambition to become a pilot. However, zie struggled to accept the physical changes in zir body during adolescence which created mental distress in zir. Zie was restricted from climbing trees and playing cricket like boys despite zir interest. “I was afraid to reveal who I am.

At the age of 12, when I had discovered my identity, what frightened me the most were my surroundings and my family.” These are the words of Adam Harry, India’s first trans man pilot. Upon realizing zir identity, Adam felt alienated at the girls only school. Humiliation and exclusion from activities zie once enjoyed put zir in great mental pressure. However, zir dream of becoming a pilot served as a beacon of inspiration.

Eventhough at the age of 17, zie joined a course to become a private pilot in Johannesburg, zie had to face numerous obstacles along zir studies, one of which was due to the revelation of zir true identity. Due to financial crisis, zie worked in restaurants, slept in open areas, and studied in public libraries. Despite his challenging circumstances, zie excelled in exams. However, due to economic constraints, zie had to return home after a year and ended up in house arrest. Zie was also exposed to both physical and mental torture and was even taken to the hospital. One day, zie left home with only a pair of clothes and got enrolled in an aviation academy. However, zie was forced to quit when they discovered that zie was a trans man. While zie was employed at a juice shop operated by 'Kudumbashree', news about zir spread on social media.

A female officer from the Child Welfare Department noticed this and advised zir to seek assistance from the Department of Social Justice. Zie received a scholarship and support from the Department of Social Justice. This was a turning point in Adam’s life. Zie faced challenges in securing employment in the aviation sector solely because zie is a trans man. After submitting an application to the Ministry of Civil Aviation followed by several interventions, the Director General issued circulars and directives regarding medical examination procedures related to transgenders. These directives aimed to ensure fairness and inclusivity in the aviation sector for transgenders. During the training programs in Johannesburg as a commercial pilot, Adam Harry had been actively involved in various social activities many of which addressed gender minority problems.

Adam Harry's persistence and eventual success in overcoming obstacles, particularly in the face of significant societal challenges, are considered commendable achievements. There will be similar people in your neighbourhood who have fought against all odds. How could they achieve it?
